name: Top spenders by domain
description: All-in cost per store: model spend plus search-data spend, never model spend alone. A store that looks cheap on the model chart can be expensive on search data, and the two are billed by different vendors.

name: Cost per published article
description: What one article cost us all-in, stamped when it shipped. The split between the two vendors travels with it, so an unusually expensive article can be explained rather than just noticed.

name: Model vs search-data split
description: Which vendor the money actually goes to, product-wide. The number that says whether a cost problem is a prompt problem or a query-volume problem.

name: Search-data spend per day
description: Everything the search-data vendor billed us each day, for every request whoever it was made for, failed requests included — the vendor charges for work done, not answers received. The same record the daily cap is counted from.

name: Cost per domain
description: Top spenders, cost per published article by domain, and the split between the model vendor and the search-data vendor. Always both — LLM-only is the number that misleads.

name: A domain's daily model spend is over its cap
description: Mirrors the per-account trip in our own code, so a human sees what the code already acted on. This alert never causes the pause; the sweep reading our own ledger does.

name: Global daily search-data spend is over its cap
description: The vendor bill is one bill, so this ceiling is product-wide. Mirrors the global trip. It watches today as it accumulates, not just finished days: spend only ever goes up within a day, so a partial day over the cap is already over it.
